The study enrolls 60 patients per group and aims to detect a 10 mm Hg difference in systolic blood pressure between the new drug and placebo, with a preset alpha of 0.05.
At the end of the trial, the mean reduction in systolic blood pressure for the drug group is 7 mm Hg, while the placebo group has a mean reduction of 2 mm Hg (p = 0.08).
The investigators conclude that the new drug does not result in a statistically significant reduction in blood pressure compared to placebo.
However, a larger subsequent trial with 400 patients per group detects a difference of 7 mm Hg (p = 0.01) and concludes the drug is effective.

encounters.cc: Progressive paresthesia and neuropathy three days after new chemotherapy infusion

lines: Progressive paresthesia and neuropathy three days after new chemotherapy infusion

The patient is a 56-year-old female with stage 5 chronic kidney disease on maintenance hemodialysis, seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, and prior neurological conditions including trigeminal neuralgia and Ramsay Hunt syndrome, who returns to the oncology clinic for evaluation of progressive paresthesia.
She was diagnosed 14 months ago and initially treated with optimal cytoreductive surgery followed by a platinum-based regimen, but her disease progressed after 2 additional lines of chemotherapy.
Her oncologist started her on a new agent targeting rapidly dividing cells.
She now reports progressive tingling, numbness, and burning pain in her toes and fingertips, which have been gradually ascending over the past 48 hours.
She also notes mild weakness when climbing stairs, generalized fatigue, and increased hair shedding.
